findings.title: Basis for Award
findings.fact: Awards will be made to the responsive and responsible Contractor(s) with the highest Total Financial Score per Configuration that meets all specified technical requirements.
findings.business_implication: The award is based solely on the highest Total Financial Score, which is determined by lowest cost. Technical requirements are pass/fail, so price is the differentiator. This means competitive pricing is crucial to win.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a pricing strategy that offers aggressive discounts while ensuring all technical requirements are met. Focus on providing the lowest total cost for each configuration to maximize the financial score.

quotes.quote: BASIS FOR AWARD Highest Total Financial Score meeting specified Technical Requirements and Mandatory Pass/Fail Requirements.
Awards will be made to the responsive and responsible Contractor(s) with the highest Total Financial Score per Configuration that meets all the specified technical requirements.

findings.title: Evaluation Process Stages
findings.fact: The evaluation is a three-stage process: Stage 1 Administrative Review, Stage 2 Technical Evaluation, and Stage 3 Financial Evaluation.
findings.business_implication: The evaluation is sequential; failure in any stage eliminates the bid. Administrative completeness and technical compliance are prerequisites for financial evaluation. Therefore, attention to detail in all stages is essential.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all required documents are complete and in the original format to pass Stage 1. Verify that all proposed SKUs are on the approved price list and meet technical specs for Stage 2. Only then focus on pricing for Stage 3.

quotes.quote: The evaluation is a three-stage process set forth below:
5.1.1 STAGE 1 ADMINISTRATIVE REVIEW
5.1.2 STAGE 2 TECHNICAL EVALUATION OF CONFIGURATION SUBMISSION
5.1.3 STAGE 3 FINANCIAL EVALUATION

findings.title: Evaluation Weights
findings.fact: Technical Response is Pass/Fail, Financial Response is 100% of evaluation. Total Financial Score is based on lowest cost with points: Standard Configuration 50 points, Required Products: Warranty/Services 15 points, Components 30 points, Peripherals 5 points.
findings.business_implication: Since technical is only pass/fail, the entire competitive differentiation rests on pricing. The financial score is heavily weighted towards the standard configuration (50 points) and components (30 points), so pricing on these items will have the most impact on the overall score.
findings.action_recommendation: Focus on aggressive pricing for the standard configuration and components, as they carry the most weight. Ensure technical compliance to pass the technical gate, but allocate more effort to cost optimization.

quotes.quote: Technical Response (Attachment A – Technical Response, Attachment D – Issue Escalation Plan, and Manufacturer Information Page): Pass/Fail    Financial Response : 100%

Total Financial Score is based on lowest cost and the points are weighted as follows: • Standard Configuration - 50 points • Required Products o Warranty/Services - 15 points o Components - 30 points o Peripherals - 5 points

findings.title: Stage 1 Administrative Review
findings.fact: Attachment A, Attachment D, and Manufacturer Information page are reviewed for completeness. Alterations to documents are prohibited and may result in rejection.
findings.business_implication: Any modification to the provided documents, such as adding/deleting worksheets, unlocking, or rewriting formulas, can lead to immediate rejection. This is a strict compliance requirement that must be met to avoid disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all required documents are fully completed without any alterations. Use the original templates and do not change any formatting or formulas. Double-check that all fields are filled before submission.

quotes.quote: The submitted Attachment A – Technical Response, Attachment D – Issue Escalation Plan, and the Manufacturer Information page (last page of this document) will be reviewed for completeness. The addition or deletion of worksheets, columns, unlocking the document, rewriting formulas, or similar alterations to any document is prohibited. OGS reserves the right to reject any Contractor Submission or portion(s) thereof determined to have been altered/modified by the Contractor from the original format. Failure to provide fully completed documents may result in rejection of the RFQ Response without further review.

findings.title: Stage 2 Technical Evaluation
findings.fact: Attachment A is compared to Standard Configuration and Required Products requirements. SKUs must be on the Contractor's approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List; otherwise, the configuration may not proceed.
findings.business_implication: If any proposed SKU is not on the approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List, the entire configuration may be disqualified from further evaluation. This is a critical gatekeeper for technical compliance.
findings.action_recommendation: Before submission, verify that all SKUs listed in Attachment A are on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List. If any are missing, either add them to the contract or replace them with approved alternatives. Prioritize contract modification requests if needed.

quotes.quote: Submitted Attachment A – Technical Response will be compared to Standard Configuration and Required Products requirements. All proposed SKUs for proposed products offered in Attachment A – Technical Response must be on the Contractor’s approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List. Any Configuration that contains a SKU that is not included on the Manufacturer’s Umbrella Contract Price List may not proceed further in the evaluation process.

findings.title: Stage 3 Financial Evaluation
findings.fact: Only Contractors whose Standard Configuration specifications and Required Products pass review proceed to financial evaluation. Attachment C is used for pricing evaluation.
findings.business_implication: Financial evaluation is only open to those who pass technical review. This means that technical compliance is a prerequisite for being considered for award, and pricing is only evaluated after technical acceptance.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure technical requirements are fully met to advance to the financial stage. Once technical is passed, focus on preparing competitive pricing in Attachment C, as it will be the sole basis for scoring.

quotes.quote: Only Contractors whose Standard Configuration specifications and Required Products pass review, as determined by OGS, will proceed to the evaluation of Attachment C – Financial Response for those specific Configurations. For those Contractors who have been determined to have passed the Technical Evaluation, their Attachment A - Technical Response will be used to create the Attachment C – Financial Response and be provided to the Contractor in order to complete and submit. The proposed pricing on Attachment C – Financial Response will then be used in the Financial Evaluation.

findings.title: Mandatory Products
findings.fact: All components within Standard Configuration and Required Products are mandatory. Failure to complete required fields may result in rejection.
findings.business_implication: Incomplete submissions, whether in technical or financial attachments, can lead to outright rejection without further review. This underscores the importance of thoroughness and accuracy in all required fields.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct a comprehensive review of all mandatory fields in both Attachment A and Attachment C. Ensure every required component is included and all fields are filled out completely. Use checklists to verify completeness before submission.

quotes.quote: ALL COMPONENTS WITHIN THE STANDARD CONFIGURATION AND ITS REQUIRED PRODUCTS ARE MANDATORY. Failure to complete all required fields in Attachment A – Technical Response or Attachment C – Financial Response may result in rejection of the RFQ Response without further review.

findings.title: Pricing Requirements
findings.fact: Quoted pricing must not exceed Net NYS Contract Price on Manufacturer's Umbrella Contract. Pricing on Attachment C must be equal to or better than Manufacturer Umbrella Contract pricing.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that all pricing submitted in Attachment C is at or below the established Net NYS Contract Price from the Manufacturer's Umbrella Contract. Failure to comply could lead to disqualification or rejection of the bid.
findings.action_recommendation: Before submission, verify that every SKU's quoted price on Attachment C is equal to or lower than the corresponding Net NYS Contract Price on the Manufacturer's Umbrella Contract. Implement a review process to cross-check all line items.

quotes.quote: All pricing offered on Attachment C - Financial Response must be equal to or better than the pricing offered for that SKU on the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract.
In no event may quoted pricing exceed the Net NYS Contract Price on the Manufacturer’s Umbrella Contract.

findings.title: Evaluation of Required Products Pricing
findings.fact: Pricing for Required Products will be factored into the final Quote price for evaluation.
findings.business_implication: The pricing of Required Products directly impacts the evaluation score. Aggressive discounts on these items can improve the bid's competitiveness.
findings.action_recommendation: Strategically set discounts for Required Products to be as low as possible while maintaining profitability, as these will be a significant factor in the final evaluation.

quotes.quote: Contractors are encouraged to aggressively discount their pricing for their Required Products, as the pricing will be factored in the final Quote price for evaluation.

findings.title: Evaluation of Standard Configuration Pricing
findings.fact: Contractors must provide itemized pricing on all Products in Standard Configurations, and pricing must not exceed the Net NYS Contract Price on the Manufacturer's Umbrella Contract.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must provide detailed pricing for every product in the Standard Configurations, and each price must be at or below the Net NYS Contract Price. Non-compliance could result in disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare itemized pricing for all Standard Configuration products, ensuring each line item is priced at or below the corresponding Net NYS Contract Price. Double-check all entries for accuracy.

quotes.quote: Contractors shall provide itemized pricing on all Products offered in the Standard Configurations. In no event may quoted pricing exceed the Net NYS Contract Price on the Manufacturer’s Umbrella Contract.

Contractors shall provide itemized pricing on all Products offered in the Standard Configurations. In no event may quoted pricing exceed the Net NYS Contract Price on the Manufacturer’s Umbrella Contract.

findings.title: Evaluation of Required Product Pricing
findings.fact: The Net NYS Contract Price for a Required Product must represent the complete price of the Product; recording the price as a difference from a line-item in the Standard Configuration is prohibited.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must list the full price for each Required Product, not a differential price. Misreporting could lead to rejection or penalties.
findings.action_recommendation: When filling out Attachment A for Required Products, ensure that the Net NYS Contract Price is the total price for the product, not a difference from another line item. Review all entries to confirm compliance.

quotes.quote: The Net NYS Contract Price provided on Attachment A – Technical Response for a Required Product must represent the complete price of the Product. Recording the price of the Product as the difference in price from a line-item in the Standard Configuration is prohibited.

findings.title: Evaluation of Required Product Discounts
findings.fact: Contractors must bid a discount percentage on the item selected for each Required Product category.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must specify a discount percentage for each Required Product category, which will be applied to the selected item and all additional products in that category. This discount affects the evaluation and future pricing.
findings.action_recommendation: Determine competitive discount percentages for each Required Product category, ensuring they are financially viable and align with the bid strategy. Clearly document these percentages in the submission.

quotes.quote: For Required Products, Contractors must bid a discount percentage on the item that has been selected for each category (e.g., a 3-button mouse for Peripherals).

findings.title: Evaluation of OGS Reserved Rights
findings.fact: OGS reserves the right to reject any or all RFQ Responses, withdraw the RFQ, award all, any number, or none of the 14 Product Configurations, disqualify any Contractor, seek clarifications, amend the RFQ, change schedule dates, eliminate non-material specifications, waive requirements, negotiate, require clarification, unilaterally make non-material revisions, exclude price lists, cure non-material issues, reject unrealistically low prices, modify products, and modify specifications prior to Financial Evaluation.
findings.business_implication: OGS has broad discretion to alter the procurement process, which introduces significant uncertainty for bidders. The ability to reject unrealistically low prices means that aggressive pricing could be disqualified, and the unilateral modification of specifications could affect the competitiveness of submitted bids.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should carefully review all RFQ requirements and ensure their responses are fully compliant to avoid disqualification. Pricing should be realistic and justifiable, not unrealistically low. Bidders should also be prepared for potential changes and maintain flexibility in their offerings.

quotes.quote: OGS reserves the right to: 1. Reject any or all RFQ Responses received in response to the RFQ;

2. Withdraw the RFQ any time, in whole or in part, in its sole discretion; 3. Award all, any number, or none of the 14 Product Configurations; 4. Disqualify any Contractor whose conduct and/or Response fails to conform to the requirements of the RFQ; 5. Seek clarifications and revisions of the RFQ response; 6. Prior to the RFQ Submission Date for Attachment C – Financial Response, amend the RFQ to correct errors or oversights, or to supply additional information, as it becomes available; 7. Prior to RFQ Submission Date for Attachment C – Financial Response, direct Contractors to submit RFQ response modifications addressing subsequent amendments; 8. Change any of the schedule dates with notification via email to all applicable Manufacturer Umbrella Contractors; 9. Eliminate any mandatory, non-material specifications that cannot be complied with by all of the prospective Contractors; 10. Waive any requirements that are not material; 11. Negotiate with a Contractor responding to this RFQ within the RFQ requirements to serve the best interests of the State. This includes requesting clarifications of any or all Contractor’s RFQ Responses; 12. Require clarification at any time during the procurement process and/or require correction of arithmetic or other apparent errors for the purpose of assuring a full and complete understanding of a Contractor’s RFQ Responses and/or to determine a Contractor’s compliance with the requirements of the RFQ; 13. Unilaterally make non-material revisions, changes and/or updates to any templates and/or Attachments to the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement without processing a formal amendment and/or modification; 14. The State reserves the right to exclude any price lists or individual Products and services that do not fall within the scope of the RFQ; 15. Upon discovery of non-material completeness or conformance issues with a Contractor’s RFQ Response, contact the Contractor to attempt to cure the issue prior to completion of the evaluation of the Contractor’s RFQ Response; 16. Reject any Bid containing proposed prices that are unrealistically low as determined by OGS; 17. Modify the Products identified in Attachment A – Technical Response prior to the prequalified Contractors’ submittal of Attachment C – Financial Response. 18. Modify a specification within the Standard Configuration or Required Product categories in Attachment A – Technical Response or Attachment C – Financial Response prior to the Financial Evaluation, upon written notice to Contractors that have submitted a quote.

findings.title: Commencement of Sales
findings.fact: Awarded Contractors can commence sales only after OGS acceptance and posting of the Aggregate Agreement and awarded Configurations on the OGS website.
findings.business_implication: There will be a delay between award notification and the ability to start selling, which could impact revenue projections and resource allocation. Contractors must not begin sales prematurely.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for a post-award period before sales can begin. Ensure internal teams are ready to launch once the agreement is posted. Monitor OGS website for the official posting date.

quotes.quote: The awarded Contractors can commence sales from the resulting Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement only upon OGS acceptance and posting of the Aggregate Agreement and awarded Configurations with the awarded Contractor(s) contact information on the OGS website.

findings.title: Estimated Spend and Quantity
findings.fact: The estimated dollar value of the aggregated award is approximately $40 million, but there is no guarantee of volume or dollar value to be purchased.
findings.business_implication: The $40 million estimate is not a commitment; actual purchases could be significantly higher or lower. This uncertainty affects capacity planning, inventory, and pricing strategy.
findings.action_recommendation: Do not base business decisions solely on the estimated spend. Prepare for variable demand by maintaining flexible supply chains and avoid over-investing in inventory. Consider the potential for higher volumes if pricing is competitive.

quotes.quote: The estimated dollar value of the aggregated award of the fourteen (14) Standard Configurations in this RFQ, based on historical purchases under previous awards, is approximately $40 million.
There is no guarantee of volume to be purchased
There is no guarantee of dollar value to be purchased

findings.title: eMarketplace Participation
findings.fact: Contractors awarded a Configuration must provide a hosted or punch-out catalog via NYS eMarketplace; no fees for mandatory participation, but optional ERP integration may incur fees.
findings.business_implication: Participation in eMarketplace is mandatory for awardees, requiring investment in catalog development and maintenance. While there is no fee for basic participation, ERP integration could add costs.
findings.action_recommendation: Budget for catalog setup and maintenance. Evaluate the benefits of ERP integration against the additional fees. Ensure the catalog is accurate and up-to-date to avoid compliance issues.

quotes.quote: Contractors that are awarded a Configuration under the Aggregate Agreement should provide a “hosted” or “punch-out” catalog that is available to Authorized Users via the NYS eMarketplace.

There are no fees required for a Contractor’s mandatory participation in the catalog site development or management. However, Contractors who wish to integrate their ERP system with the NYS eMarketplace can do so for an additional fee.

findings.title: Supply Shortage Prioritization
findings.fact: In supply shortage, contractor must prioritize NYS Authorized Users over extended customers; must contact OGS for approval before prioritizing others.
findings.business_implication: During supply shortages, NYS orders take precedence, which could strain relationships with other customers. Failure to comply could result in penalties or loss of contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a clear allocation plan for supply shortages that prioritizes NYS orders. Establish communication protocols with OGS for any exceptions. Ensure staff are trained on these requirements.

quotes.quote: In the event of a supply shortage an Awarded Contractor must make all reasonable efforts to prioritize orders placed under this originating Agreement for New York State Authorized Users, over any orders made by extension of this Agreement to customers outside of New York State Authorized Users.

In addition, in the event that the Awarded Contractor believes it necessary to prioritize orders made by extension of this Agreement to customers outside of New York State Authorized Users, over orders placed under this originating Agreement for New York State Authorized Users, the Awarded Contractor must contact OGS for approval prior to fulfilling such orders.

findings.title: Term and Extension
findings.fact: Initial term is one year, with OGS option to extend up to an additional one year; short-term extension up to 3 months unilateral, up to 6 months with contractor concurrence.
findings.business_implication: The contract duration is relatively short, with potential for extension. This creates uncertainty in revenue forecasting and resource planning. The unilateral extension clause gives OGS flexibility but may lead to abrupt changes.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for a possible one-year extension by maintaining capacity and pricing stability. Monitor OGS communications for extension notices and prepare to negotiate terms if a longer extension is desired.

quotes.quote: The term of the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement shall be one (1) year.

OGS reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to extend all or some Configurations of the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement for a period up to an additional one (1) year upon written notice to the Contractor.

In the event a replacement Agreement has not been issued, any Agreement let and awarded hereunder by the State, may be extended unilaterally by the State for an additional period of up to three (3) months upon notice to the Awarded Contractor with the same terms and conditions as the original Agreement including, but not limited to, prices and delivery requirements. With the concurrence of the Awarded Contractor, the extension may be for a period of up to six (6) months in lieu of three (3) months.

findings.title: Replacement Model for Standard Configuration
findings.fact: Entire Standard Configuration can be updated to new model with EOL proof; replacement price not exceed original; 60 days notice for EOL; if fail, OGS may award to next lowest bidder.
findings.business_implication: This clause allows for product refreshes but imposes strict price and specification constraints. Failure to comply could result in losing the configuration to a competitor, impacting revenue and market position.
findings.action_recommendation: Establish a proactive EOL monitoring process to ensure timely notification and replacement submissions. Ensure replacement models meet or exceed specs and are priced at or below original to avoid penalties.

quotes.quote: The Awarded Contractor(s) will be able to update the entire Standard Configuration(s) to a new model as long as acceptable proof of EOL is provided in writing to the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Contract Manager.

The replacement model price shall not exceed the original awarded amount for the Standard Configuration and its components; provided, however, if the replacement model costs less than the original Standard Configuration, the price shall be reduced to the lower cost.
OGS must receive notification no less than 60 calendar days before a Standard Configuration model becomes EOL.

During the term of the Agreement, should the awarded contractor fail to provide acceptable notice of EOL Standard Configuration(s); fail to submit a replacement Standard Configuration via the process outlined in Appendix 2 – Price List Modification Procedure in the timeframe referenced above; or, is unable to provide a replacement model with specifications that meet or exceed the specifications of the original awarded Configuration, OGS reserves the right to award the Configuration to the Contractor with the next lowest bid from RFQ 20-01 for that Configuration that is willing to accept the Configuration award without rebidding.

findings.title: Product Delivery
findings.fact: Delivery within 45 calendar days of PO receipt; extension to 60 days with Authorized User approval; beyond 60 days requires OGS approval and limited to industry-wide events.
findings.business_implication: Strict delivery timelines impose operational pressure. Extensions are possible but require approvals, and delays beyond 60 days are only allowed for industry-wide events, which could be difficult to prove.
findings.action_recommendation: Strengthen supply chain and logistics to consistently meet 45-day delivery. If delays are anticipated, proactively seek Authorized User approval for up to 60 days. For longer delays, document industry-wide events and seek OGS approval early.

quotes.quote: The Awarded Contractor(s) shall deliver the units ordered by an Authorized User within forty-five (45) calendar days of receipt of a Purchase Order unless either the Authorized User or OGS grants an extension of time as provided below.

If upon receipt of a Purchase Order the Awarded Contractor determines it cannot meet the 45 calendar day delivery period the Awarded Contractor may submit a written request to the Authorized User to extend the required Product delivery period to up to sixty (60) calendar days.

If an Authorized User wants to extend the delivery period beyond sixty (60) calendar days, the Authorized User may submit a written request to extend the Product delivery period beyond sixty (60) calendar days to OGS for its approval.

findings.title: Administrative Fee
findings.fact: Contractors must pay an administrative fee of 0.50% on all sales generated from the Agreement.
findings.business_implication: The administrative fee reduces net revenue from contract sales. Accurate tracking and timely payment are essential to avoid penalties and maintain good standing.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust sales tracking and reporting systems to accurately calculate and remit the 0.50% fee quarterly. Set aside funds to cover the fee and ensure compliance with payment deadlines.

quotes.quote: The awarded Contractor(s) are required to pay an Administrative Fee in the amount of point five percent (0.50%) for all sales generated from this Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement.

findings.title: Fiscal Audit Penalties
findings.fact: If administrative fees are underpaid by more than 5%, contractor must pay audit costs or three times the discrepancy, whichever is higher.
findings.business_implication: Underpayment of administrative fees by more than 5% triggers severe financial penalties, including audit costs or treble damages. This creates significant financial risk if reporting is inaccurate.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure meticulous accuracy in sales reporting and fee calculations. Conduct internal audits to verify compliance. If discrepancies are found, correct them immediately to avoid penalties.

quotes.quote: If, as a result of any such audit, Administrative Fees are determined to have been underpaid by more than five percent (5%) for the period audited, Contractor shall pay the costs of such audit or three times the discrepancy, whichever is higher.

findings.title: Delivery Delay Termination Risk
findings.fact: OGS may terminate the agreement if multiple delivery delays occur.
findings.business_implication: The bidder faces a significant risk of contract termination if it fails to meet delivery deadlines consistently. This could result in loss of revenue, damage to reputation, and potential exclusion from future opportunities with OGS.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust delivery tracking and management processes to ensure timely fulfillment. Proactively communicate any potential delays to OGS and Authorized Users, and maintain a buffer in supply chain to mitigate risks. Regularly review delivery performance metrics to identify and address issues early.

quotes.quote: If OGS becomes aware of multiple incidents of delays in delivery, OGS reserves the right to terminate the Agreement in whole or in part.

findings.title: Contractor Liability for Reseller Actions
findings.fact: Contractors remain wholly and solely responsible for the actions of Resellers acting on their behalf as part of the aggregate purchase, as well as the performance of all Products, and conformity with the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract and any agreement resulting from this RFQ.
findings.business_implication: The bidder is fully liable for any failures or misconduct by its resellers, including product performance and compliance with contract terms. This could lead to financial penalties, legal disputes, and damage to the bidder's relationship with OGS.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully select and vet resellers, ensuring they are reliable and compliant. Establish clear contractual agreements with resellers that include indemnification clauses and performance standards. Maintain oversight and regular audits of reseller activities to ensure compliance.

quotes.quote: Contractors remain wholly and solely responsible for the actions of the Resellers acting on their behalf as part of the aggregate purchase, as well as the performance of all Products, and conformity with the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract and any agreement resulting from this RFQ.

findings.title: Contractor Responsibility for Replacement of Incompatible Components
findings.fact: Replacement components within the Aggregate Hardware Buy RFQ 20-01 must be compatible with RFQ 20-01 peripherals or the Contractor will be responsible for replacement of both the component and the peripheral.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder provides replacement components that are not compatible with existing peripherals, it will incur the cost of replacing both the component and the peripheral. This could lead to significant financial losses and customer dissatisfaction.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure thorough compatibility testing of all replacement components before offering them. Maintain a comprehensive list of compatible components and peripherals. In case of any doubt, consult with OGS or the manufacturer to verify compatibility.

quotes.quote: Replacement components within the Aggregate Hardware Buy RFQ 20-01 must be compatible with RFQ 20-01 peripherals or the Contractor will be responsible for replacement of both the component and the peripheral.

findings.title: Contractor Liability for Reporting Inaccuracies
findings.fact: If inaccuracies of more than 5% are found in any of the reporting documents, Contractors shall pay the cost of such audit or three times the discrepancy, whichever is higher.
findings.business_implication: The bidder faces severe financial penalties if its reporting documents contain inaccuracies exceeding 5%. This could result in substantial costs and damage to the bidder's credibility with OGS.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement rigorous internal controls and verification processes for all reporting documents. Double-check calculations and data entry to ensure accuracy. Consider engaging an independent auditor to review reports before submission to minimize errors.

quotes.quote: As a result of such review, if inaccuracies of more than 5% are found in any of the reporting documents, Contractors shall pay the cost of such audit or three times the discrepancy, whichever is higher.

findings.title: Contractor Responsibility for Network Integrity
findings.fact: Connections to the Authorized User’s networks must be performed in a manner prescribed by an Authorized User to preserve the integrity of the Authorized User’s network, confidentiality and integrity of information transmitted over that Authorized User’s network, and the availability of the network.
findings.business_implication: The bidder is responsible for ensuring that any network connections it makes do not compromise the security or availability of the Authorized User's network. Failure to comply could lead to security breaches, legal liability, and loss of trust.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop and implement strict network connection procedures that align with the Authorized User's requirements. Ensure all technical staff are trained on these procedures and on relevant security standards. Obtain explicit approval from the Authorized User before making any connections and document all actions.

quotes.quote: Connections to the Authorized User’s networks must be performed in a manner prescribed by an Authorized User to preserve the integrity of the Authorized User’s network, confidentiality and integrity of information transmitted over that Authorized User’s network, and the availability of the network.

findings.title: Contractor Responsibility for Data Storage Device Custody
findings.fact: The data storage device or, if not removable, the entire unit, must remain in the custody and ownership of the Authorized User after the Contractor has completed the repair or replacement of the unit.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must ensure that any data storage devices or entire units containing data remain with the customer after service, which may impact the contractor's ability to reuse or resell such parts and may require secure handling procedures to protect customer data.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement internal processes to ensure that data storage devices are not retained after repair or replacement, and establish data sanitization or return procedures to comply with this requirement.

quotes.quote: The data storage device or, if not removable, the entire unit, must remain in the custody and ownership of the Authorized User after the Contractor has completed the repair or replacement of the unit.

findings.title: Contractor Responsibility for Remote Access Supervision
findings.fact: Access for remote diagnosis must be approved and supervised by the Authorized User’s technical representative for each specific incident.
findings.business_implication: Remote diagnostic sessions will require coordination with the customer's technical staff, potentially causing delays in troubleshooting and increasing administrative overhead for the contractor.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a process for scheduling remote sessions with customer approval, and ensure that all remote access activities are logged and supervised to comply with this requirement.

quotes.quote: Access for remote diagnosis must be approved and supervised by the Authorized User’s technical representative for each specific incident.

findings.title: Contractor Responsibility for Product Removal Due to Export Restrictions
findings.fact: If Contractor cannot deliver a Product because either the Contractor or a supplier to the Contractor is listed on any of these lists, the Contractor must remove the Product from the Contractor’s Aggregate Buy Price List.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must continuously monitor restricted party lists and be prepared to remove products from its price list if a supplier becomes listed, which could disrupt product availability and affect customer orders.
findings.action_recommendation: Establish a compliance monitoring system to screen suppliers against restricted party lists, and have contingency plans in place to quickly update the price list and communicate with customers about product unavailability.

quotes.quote: If Contractor cannot deliver a Product because either the Contractor or a supplier to the Contractor is listed on the on any of these lists, the Contractor must remove the Product from the Contractor’s Aggregate Buy Price List.

findings.title: Contractor Responsibility for Replacement Product in Export Restriction Cases
findings.fact: For any order that cannot be fulfilled as a result of such listing, the Authorized User, at their discretion, may either terminate the order or allow Contractor to fulfill the order with a replacement product that either meets or exceeds the applicable Product Specifications.
findings.business_implication: In cases where a product cannot be delivered due to export restrictions, the contractor may be required to offer a replacement product that meets or exceeds specifications, which could impact profitability and customer satisfaction.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare a list of potential replacement products that meet or exceed specifications, and establish a process for proposing replacements to customers when original products become unavailable.

quotes.quote: Additionally, for any order that cannot be fulfilled as a result of such listing, the Authorized User, at their discretion, may either terminate the order or allow Contractor to fulfill the order with a replacement product that either meets or exceeds the applicable Product Specifications.

findings.title: Contractor Responsibility for Website Accuracy
findings.fact: The Contractor’s website will be the responsibility of the Contractor to maintain and keep updated. This website must remain accurate and available throughout the duration of Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement.
findings.business_implication: The contractor is obligated to maintain an accurate and available website for the duration of the agreement, which may require ongoing investment in web maintenance and content updates.
findings.action_recommendation: Allocate resources for regular website maintenance and content updates, and implement a review process to ensure accuracy and availability throughout the contract term.

quotes.quote: The Contractor’s website will be the responsibility of the Contractor to maintain and keep updated. This website must remain accurate and available throughout the duration of Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement.

findings.title: Contractor Responsibility for Website Conflicts
findings.fact: Any conflicts between the OGS-posted price lists and items on a Contractor’s dedicated website shall be resolved in favor of the OGS-posted price list at time of the sale. Repeated conflicts between the two websites may at OGS’ discretion lead to the revoking of the ability of the Contractor to host their own dedicated website.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must ensure that its dedicated website consistently reflects the OGS-posted price lists to avoid conflicts. Failure to do so could result in loss of the ability to host its own website, which may impact sales channels and customer convenience.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a process to regularly synchronize the contractor's website with OGS price lists, and conduct periodic audits to ensure consistency. If conflicts are identified, correct them promptly to avoid OGS intervention.

quotes.quote: Any conflicts between the OGS-posted price lists and items on a Contractor’s dedicated website shall be resolved in favor of the OGS-posted price list at time of the sale. Repeated conflicts between the two websites may at OGS’ discretion lead to the revoking of the ability of the Contractor to host their own dedicated website.

findings.title: Contractor Responsibility for Advertising Compliance
findings.fact: Awarded Contractors are reminded of the requirements set forth in the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract, Appendix B General Specifications - Advertising Results, incorporated as part of the Contract, that any awarded Contractor(s) press or media releases, advertisements, or promotional literature, regardless of the medium, referring to an awarded Contractor(s) must be reviewed and approved by OGS prior to issuance.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must obtain OGS approval before issuing any press releases, advertisements, or promotional materials that reference the contract. Unapproved advertising could lead to compliance issues and potential penalties.
findings.action_recommendation: Establish an internal review process to ensure all advertising and promotional materials are submitted to OGS for approval prior to release. Maintain records of approvals for audit purposes.

quotes.quote: Awarded Contractors are remined of the requirements set forth in the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract, Appendix B General Specifications - Advertising Results, incorporated as part of the Contract, that any awarded Contractor(s) press or media releases, advertisements, or promotional literature, regardless of the medium, referring to an awarded Contractor(s) must be reviewed and approved by OGS prior to issuance.

findings.title: Contractor Responsibility for Trademark Use
findings.fact: The awarded Contractor(s) also cannot use, for any purpose, the New York State of Opportunity registered trademark or the State coat of arms without prior approval from the State.
findings.business_implication: Unauthorized use of New York State trademarks or coat of arms could result in legal liability and damage the contractor's relationship with the State.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that all marketing and promotional materials do not use the New York State of Opportunity trademark or State coat of arms without explicit prior approval from the State. Implement a review process to prevent inadvertent use.

quotes.quote: The awarded Contractor(s) also cannot use, for any purpose, the New York State of Opportunity registered trademark or the State coat of arms without prior approval from the State.

findings.title: Term and Extension Provisions
findings.fact: The Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement has a one-year term, with OGS having the right to extend for up to an additional one year, and a short-term extension provision allowing up to three months (or six months with contractor concurrence) if a replacement agreement has not been issued.
findings.business_implication: The contract duration is not guaranteed beyond the initial one-year term. OGS may extend the contract unilaterally for up to one additional year, and may also seek a short-term extension of up to three months (or six months with contractor consent) if a replacement agreement is not in place. This creates uncertainty in revenue forecasting and resource planning.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for potential extensions by maintaining flexibility in operations and supply chain. Monitor OGS communications regarding extension decisions and prepare to respond to extension requests promptly. Consider the possibility of a short-term extension and align internal resources accordingly.

quotes.quote: The term of the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement shall be one (1) year.  The term shall not commence until OGS execution and posting of the final executed documents to the Awarded Contractor(s).  OGS reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to extend all or some Configurations of the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement for a period up to an additional one (1) year upon written notice to the Contractor.

OGS reserves the right to seek an additional short-term extension for the Aggregate Hardware Buy 20-01 Agreement in accordance with Manufacturer Umbrella Contract, Section 5, Short Term Extension: In the event a replacement Agreement has not been issued, any Agreement let and awarded hereunder by the State, may be extended unilaterally by the State for an additional period of up to three (3) months upon notice to the Awarded Contractor with the same terms and conditions as the original Agreement including, but not limited to, prices and delivery requirements.  With the concurrence of the Awarded Contractor, the extension may be for a period of up to six (6) months in lieu of three (3) months.  However, this extension terminates should the replacement Agreement be issued in the interim.

findings.title: Termination for Failure to Submit Accurate Sales Reports
findings.fact: Failure to submit accurate sales reports on a timely basis may result in termination of the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract in whole or in part and activation of the Replacement Contractor provision.
findings.business_implication: Inaccurate or late sales reports can lead to termination of the contract, which would result in loss of business and potential financial penalties. The activation of a replacement contractor could also damage the contractor's reputation and future opportunities.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust sales reporting processes to ensure accuracy and timeliness. Assign dedicated personnel to prepare and submit reports by the due dates. Regularly audit reporting procedures to prevent errors and ensure compliance with OGS requirements.

quotes.quote: Failure to submit accurate reports on a timely basis may result in termination of the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract in whole or in part and activation 7.23 Replacement Contractor.

findings.title: Termination for Audit Underpayments
findings.fact: Failure to make payments for audit discrepancies or repeated errors on subsequent audits may lead to termination of the Agreement in whole or in part, after which OGS may award to the second-place contractor.
findings.business_implication: This clause poses a significant financial and reputational risk. If the contractor underreports sales or underpay administrative fees, it may face termination and lose the entire agreement, potentially impacting revenue and market position.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust internal controls to ensure accurate sales reporting and timely payment of administrative fees. Regularly audit sales data and fee calculations to avoid discrepancies. Maintain open communication with OGS to resolve any issues promptly.

quotes.quote: Failure to make such payments or repeated errors on subsequent audits may result in the scheduling of a responsibility meeting in relation to Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract, and may lead to termination of this Agreement in whole or in part, after which OGS reserves the right to award to the second-place contractor.

findings.title: Conflict in Reseller Participation: RFQ states Resellers not eligible to respond, but Section 7.10 allows use of Resellers for fulfillment
findings.fact: The RFQ states that Resellers are not eligible to respond and any bids from a Reseller will be disqualified, but later allows Contractors to use Resellers in the fulfillment of orders.
findings.business_implication: This contradiction could lead to confusion about the role of resellers. While the contractor cannot submit a bid as a reseller, they can use resellers to fulfill orders. This may affect the contractor's bidding strategy and operational planning.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with OGS the exact interpretation of reseller eligibility and usage. Ensure that the bid is submitted directly by the contractor, not through a reseller, and that any resellers used for fulfillment are properly managed and compliant with the agreement.

quotes.quote: Quotes under RFQ 20-01 will only be accepted from Lot 2 Contractors on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract; Resellers are not eligible to respond and any bids from a Reseller will be disqualified.
Contractors are permitted to use Resellers in the fulfillment of orders under any resulting Aggregate Agreement.

findings.title: Delivery Delay Reporting Requirement Ambiguity
findings.fact: The RFQ requires the contractor to submit a monthly report of any delays in delivery, but also requires the contractor to submit a report of any deliveries that fall outside the 45-day period along with the quarterly sales report. This creates ambiguity regarding the frequency and timing of delay reporting.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity in reporting requirements could lead to non-compliance and potential penalties. The contractor may inadvertently miss a required report or submit it at the wrong time, risking termination or other sanctions.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from OGS on the exact reporting schedule and format for delivery delays. Implement a system to track all delivery delays and ensure both monthly and quarterly reports are submitted accurately and on time.

quotes.quote: Contractor shall submit a monthly report to OGS of any delays in delivery by using Appendix 5.
Contractor must submit, along with Appendix 1 – Sales Report Form, a report of any and all deliveries that fall outside the 45-day period stated in Section 7.14 Product Delivery.

findings.title: Imaging Delivery Timeframe Ambiguity
findings.fact: The RFQ states that the contractor must deliver imaged units within 30 calendar days from the date of Authorized User's written approval of the test unit, but also states that the delivery date shall not be required to be less than 45 days from the date of Purchase Order. This creates ambiguity regarding the actual delivery deadline.
findings.business_implication: The conflicting delivery timeframes could lead to disputes with Authorized Users and potential breach of contract. The contractor may be held to a stricter 30-day deadline, which could be challenging to meet, or may face penalties for late delivery.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with OGS the intended delivery timeline for imaged units. Ensure that the contract clearly defines the delivery obligation and that the contractor's internal processes can meet the most stringent requirement. Communicate any potential delays to Authorized Users proactively.

quotes.quote: The Awarded Contractor(s) must deliver the remainder of the imaged units ordered by the Authorized User, within thirty (30) calendar days from the date of Authorized User’s written approval of the test unit.
Notwithstanding the foregoing in this clause the delivery date shall not be required to be less than 45 days from date of Purchase Order.
